title: TEN BILLION, HOW MANY MEGAWATTS
note: Burgum's figures are attributed to him. The film makes no claim about where a data center would be built, who is building it, or how many megawatts it would need. The closing read is the film's own opinion.

lines.text: Ten billion dollars. How many megawatts?
lines.t: Ten billion dollars. How many megawatts?

lines.text: On Wednesday, October fourteenth, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum told a Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce crowd that people are knocking on his door to drop ten billion on a data center, with no tax breaks.
lines.t: On Wednesday, October fourteenth, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum told a Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce crowd that people are knocking on his door to drop ten billion on a data center, with no tax breaks.

lines.text: He said, you convert electricity into intelligence, you make money.
lines.t: He said, you convert electricity into intelligence, you make money.

lines.text: At that event, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democratic candidate for Alaska governor, was in the audience. He said, I think we should pause.
lines.t: At that event, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democratic candidate for Alaska governor, was in the audience. He said, I think we should pause.

lines.text: Pause for what? Two days earlier, on Monday, the power company Golden Valley Electric sent a level two alert, its first under a new alert system.
lines.t: Pause for what? Two days earlier, on Monday, the power company Golden Valley Electric sent a level two alert, its first under a new alert system.

lines.text: A power company keeps spare room above what everyone's using. That's the reserve. Level two means that spare room is under fifteen megawatts.

lines.text: It happened because one generating unit went offline while two others were in scheduled maintenance. Spokesperson Ashley Bradish said the generation system is not going to be a quick fix.

lines.text: Here's the best case for yes. Burgum pointed to Ellendale, North Dakota, with homes and electric bill rebates, per K T U U.
lines.t: Here's the best case for yes. Burgum pointed to Ellendale, North Dakota, with homes and electric bill rebates, per K T U U.

lines.text: The best version is a customer that brings its own power, which could leave more reserve, not less. But the reports don't say whether this one would.
lines.t: The best version is a customer that brings its own power, which could leave more reserve, not less. But the reports don't say whether this one would.

lines.text: Kreiss-Tomkins also said, and then, in a thoughtful way, development can proceed.
lines.t: Kreiss-Tomkins also said, and then, in a thoughtful way, development can proceed.

lines.text: So every term of yes is a megawatt question, and the reports name no megawatts.
lines.t: So every term of yes is a megawatt question, and the reports name no megawatts.

lines.text: Burgum's own sentence, electricity into intelligence, makes the AI question a power question first.

lines.text: So, ten billion dollars. How many megawatts? Name them, and anyone can read the scale.
